create.title: Smooth critical radial sectors transfer to terminal M1 blocks
create.statement_tex: Let R=X^(1/4), Y=sqrt X, and let V be any fixed smooth compactly supported function in (c,C), with 0<c<C<16. For the exact Round-14 angular coefficient C_X^*(n), define G_V(X)=sum_(n<=16Y) V(n/Y) C_X^*(n)n^(-3/4)e(sqrt(Xn)). Then |G_V(X)|<<_(epsilon,V)X^epsilon. Indeed the positive reciprocal antecedent B_(j,V)=sum_h eta_j(h)1_(h<=H_j)Phi(h/(H_j+1))/h sum_d chi_4(d)w_j(d)V(4Xh^2/(d^2Y))e(hX/d) is terminal-supported; Mellin separation gives frequency BV O_V((1+|t|)/H_j) and bounded denominator coefficient, hence sum_j B_(j,V)<<_(epsilon,V)RX^epsilon. The accepted positive-frequency interior/top transforms give sum_j B_(j,V)=(e(1/8)/i)R G_V+O_V(log^2 X), with the hard-top cotangent boundary O_V(1), exact floors, profiles, hard sample, and stars. Pairing signs yields the required real GAR projection with coefficient -4R/pi. The theorem excludes the n=16Y endpoint, sharp radial cutoffs, and n/Y tending to zero.
create.next_action: Map the remaining lower radial range n=o(sqrt X) into exact frequency scales and combine the accepted terminal and TTY regions before attacking the first uncovered band. Keep the sharp n=16sqrt X endpoint separate.

update.next_action: The fixed smooth critical radial range n asymp sqrt X is closed, even in complex modulus. Isolate the exact lower-radial phase diagram n=o(sqrt X), retain the n=16sqrt X endpoint separately, and attack the first band not already covered by the terminal or TTY theorems.
Use the proved Mellin transfer as the terminal endpoint of the lower-radial phase diagram. Do not extend it to n/Y tending to zero, where h/H_j is no longer bounded below.

The full fixed-relative-width critical sector is now closed through the primal terminal theorem. The length-R moving strip remains a distinct signed reciprocal-strip problem and should not be conflated with the smooth sector.

reject.reason: Only a positive lower radial cutoff is needed. The exact inherited factor 1_(h<=H_j) owns the upper edge, and its zero-extension jump is O(1/H_j), admissible in the terminal BV norm.

The direct terminal theorem permits arbitrary bounded complex denominator coefficients, so d^(-2it) is admissible. Transform derivatives cost only polynomial powers of t, absorbed by the Schwartz Mellin transform.

The already accepted interior and top transforms are positive-frequency complex identities before conjugate pairing. Their localized form directly gives sum_j B_(j,V)=(e(1/8)/i)R G_V+O_V(log^2 X), hence the modulus bound.
Fixed support bounded away from zero forces h asymp H_j; when n/sqrt X tends to zero this fails and the terminal loss D/L reappears. The sharp outer product endpoint also needs separate ownership.
A length-R selector is a moving joint h-d or h-r strip and is not a fixed relative-width Mellin-separable radial multiplier. Round 59's signed strip remains open.

no_change.reason: Lower/intermediate radial-frequency sectors, the sharp outer endpoint, alpha transfer, and endpoint uniformity remain open.
The smooth critical-sector theorem does not change the unconditional discrepancy exponent.

round_assessment.reason: Round 60 proves a genuinely new power-saving theorem for every fixed smooth critical radial sector by transferring it to the accepted terminal reciprocal bound. The positive-frequency identity yields the stronger complex modulus, with floors, hard top, stars, and errors audited. Full GAR and the exponent remain open.
